contractEvidence.evidence: The block-format contract defines cap as a printed caption line; transcription keeps actual caption text in a separate cap block and preserves printed cross-page caption fragments. It does not require generating a cap for every prose reference or attached figure.

Cap7 requires applicable substantive desktop/mobile display evidence, visible instructional figures, actual section-break content, and no page-wide horizontal overflow. It provides no separate obligation to author a standalone caption for a shared referenced figure. The skill also explicitly prohibits independently adding extra acceptance gates.

Lesson text and publishing belong to the lesson skill. The image skill governs instructional sizing, readable English figure labels, source fidelity, and unchanged-figure reuse. It does not prescribe a standalone lesson caption for every instructional figure.

The display contract specifies purpose, layout, widths, readable label sizing, and color. It has no required standalone caption field or requirement that manifest identity labels become visible cap objects.
The quality gate requires visible English labels, adequate text size, no clipping or collision, source fidelity, and edition-text consistency. It does not add a standalone-caption gate.

proseFlow appends prose figure attachments as kind fig. It attaches existing cap objects to their uniquely identified figure, but explicitly continues when a figure group has no captions. It does not synthesize missing cap objects from figure labels.

The executed checker compares actual .figcap text against cap objects derived from proseFlow. Zero source-derived cap objects therefore require zero displayed captions here; a positive figure count does not imply a positive caption count.

independentRationale: The absence of a visible standalone caption remains a valid original pixel observation. The disputed inference was that such a caption had to exist, not whether the screenshots showed it.

Hash-verified raw, approved Chinese, English draft, and native English inventories all contain six narrative objects and zero cap objects. The modern lessons attach one shared Figure 3 through prose[0].figures; that attachment is not a caption object.

The relevant lesson contract preserves printed caption objects, while the image/display contracts require readable instructional content and labels. None imposes a standalone caption on every shared referenced figure. Native proseFlow positively permits a figure group without cap objects, corroborating rather than replacing the written contract.

The bound English draft and rendered native lesson have identical prose, including the Figure 3 reference already observed as readable in D1668. Their native flow contains 14 paragraphs, one figure, and zero captions; both D1680 views report empty captions arrays. This is source-derived agreement, not a checker bypass or a dropped caption.

The original prompt asked to judge caption placement; the clarified scope does not establish a new caption-authoring requirement. Requiring an invented standalone caption would add an unsupported gate and change source-derived lesson content.

D1668-F1 is therefore withdrawn as an invalid scope requirement. Composing that correction with the original five passing pixel checks supports PASS for the bounded saved-pixel display scope without a rerun, new content, or new science/geometry approval.
